hero.name: Juan Hernandez, PharmD
hero.title: Pharmacist-Builder · Commercial Analytics Strategist · Agentic AI

summary: Pharmacist-builder and commercial analytics strategist focused on clinician engagement, targeting, and agentic AI systems that put trusted medical information into practice. Combines hands-on product development (RAG agents, analytics agents, full-stack tools) with HCP engagement strategy (triggering, segmentation, digital/NPP target lists) in rare-disease commercial analytics at Johnson & Johnson. Early builder of a DailyMed-sourced medical AI search product (PalomaMed)—driven by a conviction that clinicians deserve fast, evidence-grounded answers at the point of care.

education.degree: Foundations of Data Science for Machine Learning
Regis Intro to Data Science / Data Engineering

experience.title: Advanced Analytics Engagement Manager
responsibilities: HCP Trigger Strategy: Identified trigger opportunities and stood up a commercial trigger strategy; trigger calls ~3.5x more effective vs. non-triggered calls, contributing an estimated +$3.3M in revenue (independently managed ~$500K project budget).

Dynamic Engagement Plan (DEP): Helped design and evolve DEP engagement targeting; DEP accounted for 21% of total brand sales. Built an adaptive-learner regression model to optimize DEP feature weights for competitor writers and current adopters (replacing manual weighting).
Predictive Targeting: Enhanced bio-naive and bio-experienced predictive models via driver/barrier analysis and new features; raised bio-naive model precision to ~60% in a rare-disease setting.
Digital / NPP Omnichannel Targeting: Owns generation of NPP email and digital engagement target lists and partners with brand to shape non-personal promotion and digital engagement strategy.

insights.ai — Commercial Analytics Agent: Built an internal analytics agent framework (skill files connected to claims and source systems) to answer target-list and claims questions—compressing work that typically took external analytics (ZS) 2-week sprints into days. Examples: trigger impact assessment in 2 days (vs. a planned 2-week ZS sprint); built and prioritized the wAIHA (next indication) target universe in-house, avoiding a $100K external analytics build.
HCP Segmentation: Designed HCP segmentation for field targeting and messaging and partnered with brand to implement it in execution.

Engagement Mix / Channel Strategy: Supported engagement strategy with spend recommendations across DTC, sales force (SF), and NPP—informing where investment drives physician and patient engagement (digital as a growing lever).
Adoption & Field Enablement: Presented analytics roadmap in POA broadcasts; ran weekly stakeholder forums and field insight sessions to drive use of targeting and engagement tools.

experience.title: Business Intelligence (BI) Manager, Market Access Insights and Analytics
experience.company: Johnson & Johnson / Rutgers Pharmaceutical Industry Fellowship
responsibilities: Led end-to-end delivery of MAIA Chat, an agentic AI search-and-summary tool for market access intelligence—from proof of concept to production use.
Built RAG data pipelines integrating SharePoint, RSS, public domain, and S3 into vector databases; shipped automated document and earnings-call summarization with NLP / agentic AI.
Built MMIT and CMS-driven dashboards and payer profiles supporting GTN and market access decision-making during PBM selling season and Medicare enrollment.
Curated insights for 250+ stakeholders; managed syndicated vendors; earned RPIF awards for AI innovation in BI.

projects.title: PalomaMed
projects.summary: Independent build of an agentic RAG product for clinicians sourcing structured drug labeling (e.g. DailyMed)—a pharmacist’s answer to slow, fragmented medical information lookup.
description: PalomaMed was an independent agentic RAG product built to help clinicians (and a veterinary use case) find and understand medication information through natural language queries, sourcing structured drug labeling such as DailyMed.
Conceived as a pharmacist’s answer to slow, fragmented medical information lookup—the same accessibility problem medical AI platforms now scale.
Product sunset after experimentation; architecture and product learning remain highly relevant to clinician-facing medical AI.
highlights: Agentic RAG over structured drug labeling (DailyMed)
Natural language query interface for clinicians
Early exploration of trusted medical information at the point of care
